title: Taylor Swift’s Toy Story 5 Song Breaks a World Record!
summary: Have you ever heard a song and just knew it would be huge? That’s exactly what happened with Taylor Swift’s new single, “I Knew It, I Knew You.” It’s from the brand-new Toy Story 5 movie, and it just blasted to No. 1 on the Billboard Global 200 chart! That’s like the world’s biggest scoreboard for songs. In its first week, the song was streamed 51.5 million times and downloaded 91,000 times. Whoa! That’s like every single person in South Korea streaming it once, with millions left over. This is Taylor’s seventh song to reach No. 1 on this chart—more than any other solo artist ever. Only the K-pop group BTS has more, with eight. The song is also the first from a Pixar movie to top the chart. The only other Disney animated film to do it was Encanto with “We Don’t Talk About Bruno.” Taylor even performed it live at the movie’s Hollywood premiere. She’s now got 15 No. 1 hits on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100, too. Talk about a winning streak! Toy Story 5 hits theaters on June 19. So grab your popcorn and listen for that song—you’ll be hearing it everywhere.
why_it_matters: When a song from a movie you love becomes a huge hit, it can feel like you're part of a global community of fans, all sharing the excitement.

keywords.explanation: A single is a music release with one main song, often to promote an album or movie.
A chart is a list that ranks songs, albums, or other things by popularity.
Streamed means listening to music or watching video online without downloading it permanently.
Downloaded means saving a copy of a file, like a song, to your device.
A premiere is the first public showing of a movie or performance.
A solo artist is a musician who performs alone, not as part of a band or group.

background_read: The Billboard Global 200 chart was launched in 2020 and ranks songs from over 200 countries based on streaming and sales data.
Taylor Swift (born 1989) started as a country singer and has become one of the world's best-selling pop artists.
South Korea (where K-pop group BTS is from) has about 51 million people, so 51.5 million streams is like everyone in that country listening once.
Article_Structure: WHAT: Her song 'I Knew It, I Knew You' from Toy Story 5 broke the record for most No.1s by a solo artist on the Billboard Global 200, getting 51.5 million streams in its first week.
WHERE: The song is from the movie Toy Story 5, and she performed it at the movie's Hollywood premiere.
WHY: Because so many people streamed and downloaded the song, it shot to the top of the charts, making it a worldwide hit.

perspectives.description: Fans are thrilled that Taylor Swift has set another record and that a Pixar song is getting so much attention.
Some might argue the song’s success is more because of the popularity of Toy Story 5 and Taylor Swift’s fame than the song’s quality.
This shows how movie soundtracks can now compete with regular pop songs in the charts, reflecting how people discover music through films.
